name: Ulm
label: Weststadt, Ulm
view: From the Neu-Ulm bank of the Danube near the Herdbruecke, looking north-west across the river at Ulm's old town. The Minster rises behind the Danube city wall: the 161.5 m west tower is on the left and the nave with its flying-buttress pinnacles runs right to the twin choir towers and the apse (side elevation, 1 m = 0.6 dp). To the left, the leaning Metzgerturm stands among the Fischerviertel gables behind the wall (1 m = 0.72 dp; its 3.3 degree lean is drawn at 4 degrees so it reads at phone size). Behind them are old-town roofs and a low Swabian Alb ridge (Kuhberg, Michelsberg), with a big tree on the Neu-Ulm bank in the foreground. By day the Danube shows a glint; at night the floodlit Minster and the promenade lamps reflect in it.
landmarks: Ulm Minster west tower (161.5 m; galleries at 70, 102 and 143 m; openwork crocketed spire)
Ulm Minster nave and choir (123.6 m long)
Metzgerturm (36 m, leaning 2.05 m to the north-west)
